thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: unusual outbound log forwarding detected from service 'logshipper-prod' to an external S3-like endpoint (suspicious-bucket[.]storage). Pattern matches recent shadow-forwarding signatures.
jamie_oncall: Thanks. Paging eng-sre + security. I'm on it — putting a priority tag.
riley_eng-sre: pulling logs, give me 2m. any obvious customer impact?
maya_security: initial glance shows only internal collector keys used. No customer identifiers in object names yet but objects contain raw request headers. Need containment asap.
jamie_oncall: Agreed. First action: block egress for logshipper-prod's task role and revoke its long-lived keys. Riley, can you attach a deny policy to the node group?
riley_eng-sre: on it. Running quick ACL patch now.
```
# deny outbound to suspicious-bucket
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name logshipper-prod-role --policy-name deny-external-s3 --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Action":"s3:*","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::suspicious-bucket/*"}]}'
```
jamie_oncall: Good. Maya, start key rotation plan for the collector service principal. We should rotate both service keys and the downstream Kinesis/API keys that logshipper used.
maya_security: Preparing rotation. Estimated 15m to generate new creds and push. Will coordinate with DevOps to avoid dropping live telemetry.
devops-jen: I can push ephemeral creds behind a feature-flag rollout. Plan: disable current shipper process, apply new env vars, restart with backfill off.
riley_eng-sre: Confirmed ACL applied. I also pushed an iptables rule on the 3 nodes still running old containers to block outbound 443 to suspicious-bucket IP range.
jamie_oncall: Nice. What's scope? Did any objects actually go external?
maya_security: We see ~142 PUTs from logshipper-prod in the 5m window. Object names look auto-generated: logs/2026-03-16/collector/xxxxx.json. Need to identify owner tenants.
jamie_oncall: Tagging customers-signal to check for PII leakage. Also legal on standby. @legal-alex please advise on notification thresholds.
legal-alex: On it. If any customer PII is confirmed, we follow the standard incident disclosure timeline. Keep me updated with list of affected accounts.
riley_eng-sre: Running quick grep to correlate object payloads to customer IDs. If payloads are raw request headers, we may have headers with x-customer-id or subdomain flags.
```
# quick grep example (sanitized)
grep -o "x-customer-id:[0-9]\+" /var/tmp/downloaded_objects/* | sort | uniq -c
```
jamie_oncall: Don't download more objects than necessary. Prefer searching on metadata via S3 list-objects + HEAD to avoid fetching PII.
maya_security: Good call. I'm enumerating keys via HEAD. Found 3 unique customer IDs in the metadata for objects in the suspicious bucket. Marking as likely impacted until we confirm.
devops-jen: Starting a controlled restart of logshipper-prod with new creds behind the flag. Rolling over 1 instance every 30s to avoid telemetry blackout.
riley_eng-sre: While that happens, I'm snapshotting current node images and saving kernel logs. Also opening a temporary honeypot to collect any further egress patterns.
jamie_oncall: Pager duty: escalate to next-level SRE if rotations fail. I'll update status page draft.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0316-57 "shadow-log-forwarding". Severity: high. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/shadow-log-forwarding
maya_security: Forensics note: preserve the original container images and the environment variables for the three nodes that did the PUTs. We'll need a full chain-of-custody for legal.
legal-alex: Received. Keep all evidence intact. No database restores without approval.
riley_eng-sre: New creds pushed, and shipper processes are restarting. 2/5 nodes completed. No additional PUTs since ACL applied.
jamie_oncall: Great. Can we confirm S3 bucket owner? Might be attacker-owned SaaS storage.
maya_security: Bucket owner is unknown; reverse DNS shows external provider. We requested object owner info via S3 HEAD — will try correlate with IP logs.
devops-jen: Backfill off, restart done on remaining nodes. Telemetry should be back to normal but batched to internal-only sink for now.
riley_eng-sre: Confirmed: outbound to suspicious-bucket IPs blocked at VPC egress for the cluster. No new connections in last 4m.
jamie_oncall: Customer impact assessment? Which accounts likely touched?
maya_security: Correlating object metadata with ingestion logs: prelim list is acct-8221, acct-1992, acct-4400. Need data team to verify if payloads contain identifiable info.
jamie_oncall: Notify CS for those accounts. Drafting owner message: recommend we reach out with transparent summary if PII confirmed.
legal-alex: If confirmed PII, we'll follow notification template B. Preparing so we can issue within SLA.
riley_eng-sre: Post-mortem checklist: 1) rotate service keys (done) 2) revoke any exposed short-term creds 3) enforce egress deny-by-default for collector role 4) add stricter S3 allow-list for internal buckets 5) alert on unusual external PUT rate.
maya_security: Also add prompt maskers to the collector so headers are sanitized before any shipping.
jamie_oncall: Agreed. I'll assign action items in the incident doc and own the timeline. On-call handoff in 40m to @riley_eng-sre.
incident-bot: Pager: on-call handover scheduled at 1802225775. Please acknowledge.
riley_eng-sre: Acknowledge. I'll be ready to continue if needed.
devops-jen: Final note: retained copies of the 142 objects in a locked internal bucket for triage, access audited. No further external egress.
maya_security: Triage complete for now. Marking incident as contained. Moving to mitigation -> root-cause analysis stage.
jamie_oncall: Thanks team. I'll run the postmortem template tomorrow and loop in product/security/ops. Closing chat for now — please DM if any new findings. :white_check_mark:"
